title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

reading.body:
This incident shows an autonomous vehicle system deployed in urban conditions without sufficient resilience for foreseeable disruptions. During severe traffic congestion after Fourth of July celebrations, at least a dozen Waymo vehicles ran out of battery power while stuck in gridlock, requiring towing. The company attributed the failure to traffic disruptions, high volume, and unexpected road closures, but the core problem was that vehicles were operating in conditions where they could not reach charging stations or complete their routes.

The failure occurred in the vehicles' energy planning and in the decision to keep them in service during a major public event when traffic patterns would be abnormal. One vehicle also caught fire after driving over fireworks on the street. It is not established whether the fire was caused by autonomous decision-making, damage to the vehicle, or road conditions. A human dispatcher or routing system that understood the event's traffic implications and either rerouted vehicles proactively or removed them from service could have prevented the stranding.

This represents a broader pattern: Waymo's San Francisco deployment has now experienced service failures from external disruptions, including an earlier incident where electrical outages immobilized vehicles at non-functioning traffic lights. Neither incident shows the autonomous driving system itself malfunctioning, but rather systems operating in real-world conditions their planners did not adequately prepare them for.

reports.title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

summary:
Multiple Waymo autonomous vehicles became stranded on San Francisco streets after their batteries drained during severe Fourth of July traffic congestion. The gridlock occurred following fireworks celebrations near the Golden Gate Bridge, with at least a dozen vehicles, mostly Jaguar I-PACE models, requiring towing. Waymo attributed the situation to major traffic disruptions, high traveler volume, and unexpected road closures. The company stated its roadside assistance team worked to clear the vehicles and said it is evaluating ways to improve resilience during major traffic events.

Additional complications emerged during the incident, including one vehicle catching fire after driving over fireworks on the street, though no injuries were reported. Passenger Rose Peterson described a harrowing moment when her Waymo continued driving despite fireworks being set off nearby. Mayor Daniel Lurie's office announced it will hold conversations with public and private partners to prevent similar delays during future events. This marks another challenge for Waymo in San Francisco following a December incident where an electrical outage caused some of its vehicles to stall at non-functioning traffic lights.
